one_line_description.value: Pumble is a team communication app for messages, channels, threads, files, and video/voice calls.
one_line_description.quote: Send messages and files to team members, easily find them with unlimited messages history, and start video conferencing with one click.

has_public_api.quote: Welcome to the Pumble API. Built on REST principles, this API allows you to integrate Pumble into your own app, by using the endpoints below.

api_type.quote: Built on REST principles, this API allows you to integrate Pumble into your own app, by using the endpoints below.

api_breadth.value: REST, ~46 endpoints across channels, messages, files, workspace users, workspaces, calls, and OAuth2; read-write
api_breadth.quote: If you're looking to integrate operations over users, channels, messages (list/preview, create new, update an existing one, leave reaction, reply etc.), you are in the right place.

auth_methods.quote: It's mandatory to include the token (access token issued to user/bot) and x-app-token (app token issued to your app, prefixed with 'xpat-') headers in every request

access_model.quote: Start using Pumble for free, and upgrade when you need more features.

access_notes.value: API access requires installing the API addon in a Pumble workspace and generating keys there; API operations are scoped to the workspace, user role, and permissions. The free Pumble plan exists and lists up to 3 apps & integrations (PRO up to 10), but the fetched pages do not explicitly confirm API addon availability by plan tier.
access_notes.quote: Before you can create an API key, you need to install the API addon on your Pumble workspace.

rate_limits.value: 100 requests per user per minute (per token header) and 500 per app (per x-app-token header); 429 responses include Retry-After
rate_limits.quote: Default limitation is 100 requests per user per minute (per token header) and 500 per app (per x-app-token header).

sdk_languages.quote: explaining how to use the Node SDK to avoid boilerplate code and manual API calls

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: Path-versioned v1 API under https://api-ga.pumble.com/v1/; no deprecation or sunset policy was found in the fetched documentation.
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: All the endpoints (except auth) are prefixed with the API URL: https://api-ga.pumble.com/v1/.

verdict_reason: Pumble publishes a REST Integration API reference with roughly 46 read-write endpoints covering messages, channels, files, users, workspaces, and calls. Credentials can be obtained self-serve by installing the API addon in a workspace and generating an API key, and a free Pumble plan is advertised. The vendor also operates a documented native MCP server at https://mcp.pumble.com/mcp.
open_questions: Rate-limit figures conflict: docs.pumble.com states 100 requests/user/minute and 500/app/minute, while the API addon help page states 'up to 1000 requests per minute per user'. Confirm which limit applies.
The fetched pages do not state whether the API addon is installable on the Free plan; free plans list 'up to 3 apps & integrations', which may or may not include the API addon.

Webhooks/event callbacks are not covered by the fetched SOURCES; a Pumble help article on incoming webhooks appeared in search results but was not included in the evidence bundle, so webhooks support is unverified.
No documented sandbox or test environment was found in the fetched pages.
The docs list OAuth2 endpoints (post /oauth2/access, get /oauth2/me), but the external OAuth app registration/consent flow is not clearly described in the fetched text.
Documentation text appears to be a Swagger-style reference; deeper endpoint schemas and error catalogs were not fully readable in the fetched bundle.
